If [Request-time APIs](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) are detected on the route, Next.js will fetch the resource on every request. - **`no-store`**: Next.js fetches the resource from the remote server on every request, even if Request-time APIs are not detected on the route. - **`force-cache`**: Next.js looks for a matching request in its server-side cache. Data can then be revalidated on-demand using [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag). This means uncached requests will not show fresh data between HMR refreshes. However, the cache will be cleared on navigation or full-page reloads. See the [`serverComponentsHmrCache`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/serverComponentsHmrCache) docs for more information. ### Hard refresh and caching in development In development mode, if the request includes the `cache-control: no-cache` header, `options.cache`, `options.next.revalidate`, and `options.next.tags` are ignored, and the `fetch` request is served from the source.
